text: If a man divorces his wife and she leaves him and marries another man, can he ever go back to her? Would not that land be utterly defiled? And you have played the whore with many lovers—yet you would return to me? declares the LORD.

Lift up your eyes to the barren heights and look: where have you not been violated? You sat waiting by the roadsides like a nomad in the desert, and you defiled the land with your whoring and your wickedness.

versions.text: Lift up your eyes to the barren heights and look: where have you not been violated? You sat waiting by the roadsides like a bandit in the wilderness, and you defiled the land with your whoring and your wickedness.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew כַּעֲרָבִי means "like an Arab/nomad"; "bandit" imports an interpretation not in the text. "Nomad" keeps the image while the preceding "sat waiting by the roadsides" already conveys the lying-in-wait sense.

text: So the showers were withheld, and no spring rain came. Yet you kept the brazen face of a prostitute; you refused to be ashamed.
Have you not just now called to me, "My Father, you are the friend of my youth"?
"Will he be angry forever? Will he hold his wrath to the end?" This is how you speak—while you do all the evil you can.
In the days of King Josiah the LORD said to me: Have you seen what faithless Israel has done? She went up on every high hill and under every green tree, and there she played the whore.
I thought that after she had done all this she would return to me, but she did not return. And her treacherous sister Judah saw it.
I saw that for all the adulteries of faithless Israel I had sent her away and given her a certificate of divorce. Yet her treacherous sister Judah was not afraid; she too went and played the whore.
With her reckless whoring she defiled the land, committing adultery with stone and wood.
And through all of this her treacherous sister Judah did not return to me with all her heart, but only in pretense, declares the LORD.
Then the LORD said to me: Faithless Israel has shown herself more righteous than treacherous Judah.
Go and proclaim these words toward the north: Return, faithless Israel, declares the LORD. I will not look on you in anger, for I am merciful, declares the LORD; I will not be angry forever.
Only acknowledge your guilt: you rebelled against the LORD your God, you scattered your favors among strangers under every green tree, and you did not obey my voice, declares the LORD.
Return, faithless children, declares the LORD, for I am your master. I will take you, one from a city and two from a family, and I will bring you to Zion.
I will give you shepherds after my own heart, and they will shepherd you with knowledge and understanding.

And when you have increased and multiplied in the land in those days, declares the LORD, no one will say any more, "The ark of the covenant of the LORD." It will not come to mind; no one will remember it or miss it, and it will not be made again.

At that time Jerusalem will be called the throne of the LORD, and all the nations will gather to it, to the name of the LORD in Jerusalem. No longer will they follow the stubbornness of their evil hearts.
In those days the house of Judah will join the house of Israel, and together they will come from the land of the north to the land I gave your fathers as an inheritance.

versions.text: In those days the house of Judah will walk with the house of Israel, and together they will come from the land of the north to the land I gave your fathers as their inheritance.
versions.explanation: "Your fathers... their inheritance" mixes second- and third-person reference awkwardly; "as an inheritance" reads more smoothly aloud. Also "join" better renders יֵלְכוּ ... עַל, which denotes joining rather than merely walking alongside.

text: I had said: How gladly would I set you among my children and give you a pleasant land, the most beautiful heritage of all the nations! And I thought you would call me "My Father" and never turn away from following me.
But like a wife unfaithful to her husband, so you have been unfaithful to me, house of Israel, declares the LORD.
A sound is heard on the barren heights—the weeping and pleading of the people of Israel, because they have twisted their ways and forgotten the LORD their God.
Return, faithless children; I will heal your faithlessness. "Here we are, we come to you, for you are the LORD our God.
Surely the hills are a delusion, the uproar on the mountains is a lie. Surely in the LORD our God is the salvation of Israel.
From our youth the shameful thing has devoured what our fathers toiled for—their flocks and herds, their sons and daughters.

versions.text: From our youth that shameful thing has devoured what our fathers toiled for—their flocks and herds, their sons and daughters.
versions.explanation: Hebrew הַבֹּשֶׁת has the definite article and is a set contemptuous substitute for Baal; "the shameful thing" is preferable to the vaguer "that shameful thing." A brief footnote noting that "the shameful thing" stands for Baal worship would help readers.

text: Let us lie down in our shame, and let our disgrace cover us. We have sinned against the LORD our God, we and our fathers, from our youth to this day, and we have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God."
